answer: Signed output watermarking stops Sybils in four steps. First, every deliverable carries a cipher watermark naming agent, client, job hash, so copies are spotted at once. Second, clients verify the mark before paying; unwatermarked work earns nothing. Third, marks are logged publicly, so one operator cannot sell one job twice. Fourth, fraud revokes the key and forfeits a $25 bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 keys, $25,000 in bonds, and $20,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust bends like a willow, not a pigment wash that rinses off, like a tailor whose label stays sewn into every coat.
